First verify the official duties, then judge whether one can take on element command and planning duties under the command and authorization system. The official duties are: commanding the combat operations of tank, light armored, and amphibious assault vehicle units in land or water combat environments; the duties include directing crew members in operating aiming and firing systems, coordinating the operation of advanced onboard communications and navigation equipment, commanding the transport of personnel and equipment during combat operations, developing and executing operational plans (including the tactical employment of armored vehicle units), and coordinating with infantry, artillery, and air support units. The check should center on command relationships, operational plans, and site and record evidence rather than job titles; whether command and handling are authorized is determined by the military's appointment, branch assignment, and chain of command.

Suited to people who can work under a highly procedural and command system, bear responsibility for personnel and mission outcomes, and ask for instructions and escalate through the chain of command under incomplete information and time pressure; not suited to people who treat simulation exercises, games, or film experience as real command authority.

Commissioning, branch assignment, training, and appointment are determined by the military's own system; this page does not provide recruitment standards, medical standards, or assessment content; any command and handling authorization follows the appointment and chain of command, and the output of simulations or assistive tools cannot serve as a basis for combat decisions.

In one sentence: this is a military occupation whose core duties are commanding armored vehicle elements in combat, directing crews in operating aiming and firing systems, coordinating onboard communications and navigation, commanding the transport of personnel and equipment, developing operational plans, and coordinating with infantry, artillery, and air support. Whether one is competent depends on passing appointment and training, command and planning ability, and element combat performance, not personality labels. Wage, employment, and work context data are not public for this occupation, and this page keeps the visible gaps.

entries.answer: The official duty description is: commanding the combat operations of tank, light armored, and amphibious assault vehicle units in land or water combat environments; the duties include directing crew members in operating aiming and firing systems, coordinating the operation of advanced onboard communications and navigation equipment, commanding the transport of personnel and equipment during combat operations, developing and executing operational plans (including the tactical employment of armored vehicle units), and coordinating with infantry, artillery, and air support units. Specifically, the work includes assessing the situation and forming a course of action, breaking intent and tasks into orders executable by crews and elements, organizing coordination with infantry, artillery, and air support, commanding the transport of personnel and equipment during combat operations, and completing records and reports per the military's operational and operating regulations. O*NET has not published this military occupation's task list or work context data, and this page does not add daily details unsupported by sources.
entries.question: What do armored assault vehicle officers do every day?

entries.answer: Aircraft officers execute and direct in-flight missions; launch and recovery officers manage the operation and maintenance of carrier launch and recovery systems; artillery and missile officers manage the corresponding personnel and weapon systems and cannot all be summarized as indirect fire; command center officers manage communications, detection, and weapon systems and also direct weapon computers. Infantry officers may deploy vehicle equipment; armored crews emphasize operation and maintenance, and armored officers explicitly cover unit command and operational planning. The comparison is not qualification or an exclusive division of all labor.
